title: Audit Export Settings: Console UX for destination setup, filter builder, and status/health
creator: Tessa Morgan
project: Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation — SIEM-ready audit export (Beta)
description:
Design the Redwood Console experience for SIEM-ready audit exports (beta): (1) settings page IA + flows to add/manage export destinations (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs, S3), (2) filter builder interaction model aligned with filtering ADR, and (3) delivery status/health presentation (lag, errors, last success, pause state). Include accessibility notes and content guidelines for beta limitations.

Primary personas:
- Security Ops / Detection Engineering: wants reliable export, understands delivery semantics, needs fast diagnosis when something breaks.
- Compliance / GRC: wants evidence that logs export is enabled and healthy; expects clear retention/backfill semantics.
- Platform Admin: configures destinations/credentials with least privilege; needs guardrails.

Out of scope for beta (but must be clearly messaged in UI): Private/on-prem deployments; non-Splunk/Datadog/S3 sinks; exactly-once guarantees; unlimited backfill.
acceptance_criteria: Export Settings page IA defined (entry point, empty states, list view, details view) with clear separation of: Destinations, Filters, Backfill, Health/Status, and Permissions messaging.

Filter builder interaction model supports: allowlist/denylist by category and action; optional actor/resource predicates; safe defaults; validation + error copy; includes examples for common SOC workflows.

Destination setup flows specified for Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs, and S3, including credential input patterns (secret references vs raw secrets where applicable), “Test connection” interaction, and failure messaging.
Status/Health UI spec includes: enabled/paused state, export lag, throughput (optional), last success timestamp, last error summary, and per-destination health badge with drill-down diagnostics.
Accessibility notes included (keyboard navigation, focus management, ARIA for filter chips/comboboxes, contrast requirements, and error announcement).
Beta disclaimers and guardrails included in UX content: at-least-once delivery + dedup expectations, limited backfill, and feature-flag enablement.
proposed_information_architecture:
Console > Settings (workspace) > Security & Compliance > Audit exports (Beta)

Sections:
1) Overview banner
- “Audit exports (Beta)” label + short explanation
- Workspace eligibility + feature-flag messaging (if not enabled)
- Link to docs/FAQ (internal + customer-facing where appropriate)

2) Destinations
- Table/list of configured destinations
- Primary actions: Add destination, Edit, Rotate credentials (if permitted), Pause/Resume, Delete
- Per-row badges: Healthy / Degraded / Paused / Misconfigured

3) Filters
- Summary of current filter policy (e.g., “Export ALL events” vs “Export selected categories/actions”) with Edit CTA
- Warning if filter is overly restrictive (best-effort heuristic: predicts near-zero volume)

4) Backfill / Replay
- Beta-safe backfill controls (bounded): “Backfill last N hours/days” with max limit copy
- “Request backfill” is gated by RBAC + may require support involvement (copy to be finalized w/ PM)

5) Status & diagnostics
- Export lag chart (sparkline) and current lag value
- Last successful delivery timestamp
- Last error message with standardized codes (e.g., AUTH_FAILED, THROTTLED_429, PERMISSION_DENIED, DESTINATION_UNREACHABLE)
- Link: “View exporter health details” (drilldown panel)

6) Permissions
- Inline explanation of who can manage exports; link to role docs
- If user lacks permissions: show read-only view + “Contact admin” guidance
key_user_flows:
A) First-time enablement (feature flag already on)
1. User lands on empty state
2. CTA: “Add destination”
3. Choose destination type (Splunk / Datadog / S3)
4. Configure destination fields + credentials
5. (Optional) Configure filter (defaults to ALL)
6. (Optional) Configure backfill window (defaults off)
7. Test connection
8. Save
9. Success state shows destination as “Healthy (pending first delivery)” and suggests verifying events in SIEM

B) Filter change
1. User opens Filters section > Edit
2. Select mode: Export all vs Export selected
3. If Export selected: user chooses categories/actions; optional predicates
4. Validation and “Impact” helper text (qualitative)
5. Save with confirmation modal: “May reduce visibility; ensure required categories are included”
6. Status shows “Config updated” with audit trail note (control plane emits config-change audit events)

C) Triage degraded export
1. Destination badge shows “Degraded”
2. User clicks into destination details
3. See: last success, last error, suggested action (rotate token / check index / check IAM)
4. CTA: Pause export (to stop retry storm) or Retry test connection
5. Optional: link to runbook (internal) and support handoff copy

D) Pause/resume
1. User clicks Pause
2. Confirmation modal explains effect: exporter stops sending new events; backlog grows; on resume it will catch up (at-least-once)
3. Resume triggers “catch-up” banner; UI emphasizes dedup expectations downstream
destination_setup_fields:
Splunk HEC (Beta)
- HEC endpoint URL (must be HTTPS)
- Token (secret input; masked; optional paste vs reference depending on control plane implementation)
- Index (optional; default per customer guidance)
- Source (optional)
- Sourcetype (optional; recommended default: redwood:audit)
- Compression toggle (default on)
- Test connection: sends a single synthetic “redwood.audit_export.test” event (must be labeled clearly as test)

Datadog Logs (Beta)
- Intake site/region (dropdown; e.g., US1, US3, EU1) OR explicit intake URL (advanced)
- API key (secret)
- Tags (key:value chips; e.g., env:prod, workspace:<id>)
- Service name (default: redwood-inference)
- Test connection: sends a single synthetic test event and verifies 2xx response

S3 (Beta)
- Bucket + prefix
- Region (derived or explicit)
- Auth method: (1) Assume role (cross-account) (2) Access key (if supported; discourage)
- SSE mode: SSE-S3 vs SSE-KMS
- KMS key ARN (if SSE-KMS)
- Partitioning summary (read-only): /year=/month=/day=/hour=; batching notes
- Test connection: verifies PutObject permissions with a small test object (clearly labeled and auto-cleaned where possible)
filter_builder_interaction_model:
Principles
- Safe-by-default: default is “Export all events” until customer intentionally restricts.
- Progressive disclosure: start with categories; advanced predicates are collapsed.
- Predictability: avoid free-form query language in beta; use structured selectors.

UI pattern
- Mode selector:
  ( ) Export all events
  ( ) Export selected events (recommended only if customer has strict scope)

When “Export selected” is chosen:
- Step 1: Categories (multi-select with descriptions)
  Examples: authentication, authorization, workspace_admin, api_keys, model_access, billing_admin, data_access
- Step 2: Actions (optional multi-select; scoped to chosen categories)
  Examples: create, update, delete, rotate, login_success, login_failure
- Step 3 (Advanced): Predicates
  - Actor type: human / service account (checkboxes)
  - Actor ID (exact match) (text input; warns about brittleness)
  - Resource type: workspace, model, api_key, export_destination, role_binding
  - Resource ID (exact match)

Allowlist vs denylist
- Beta recommendation: allowlist only.
- Denylist (if supported by backend) is behind an “Advanced” toggle with warning: “Use with care; may hide critical events.”

Validation and UX feedback
- Inline validation with clear error copy (e.g., “At least one category is required when exporting selected events.”)
- Readable summary sentence at top:
  “Export categories: Authentication, API Keys. Actions: Create, Delete. Actor: human.”
- Provide 2–3 clickable presets (non-binding) for common needs:
  - “Admin changes only”
  - “Authentication events”
  - “API key lifecycle”

Preview
- For beta: no live sample event preview (requires data access + complexity). Instead, show a static example payload snippet with highlighted fields and a link to schema docs.
status_and_health_presentation:
Status hierarchy
- Healthy: exporter delivering; lag within SLO; no recent adapter errors
- Degraded: delivering with elevated lag OR intermittent errors OR destination throttling
- Paused: intentionally paused by admin or auto-paused by system safety
- Misconfigured: validation failing (auth/permissions/URL) and not delivering

List view
- Badge + one-line subtitle:
  - Healthy — “Last success 2m ago”
  - Degraded — “Throttled (429). Lag: 18m”
  - Misconfigured — “Auth failed. Token rejected”

Detail drawer/page (per destination)
- Key fields:
  - Enabled/Paused toggle
  - Current lag value + trend (sparkline)
  - Last success timestamp
  - Last error (message + code) and “First seen” time
  - Retry behavior copy: “Redwood retries with backoff. Delivery is at-least-once.”
- Actions:
  - Test connection
  - Rotate credential (if permitted)
  - Pause/Resume
  - Delete

Content requirements (beta)
- Must clearly state: “At-least-once delivery. Your SIEM should deduplicate using event_id.”
- Must mention bounded backfill and the expected time to catch up after downtime.
accessibility_notes:
Keyboard and focus
- All destination type cards and primary CTAs reachable via keyboard; visible focus ring.
- Filter multi-selects must support keyboard navigation (arrow keys) and typeahead.
- Chip lists (selected categories/tags) must be removable via keyboard (Backspace/Delete) and have clear focus order.

ARIA and screen reader support
- Comboboxes: use ARIA 1.2 combobox pattern; announce selection count changes.
- Inline validation: error text associated with inputs via aria-describedby; errors announced on submit.
- Status badges: include text labels (not color-only) and sr-only expansions for icons.

Color and contrast
- Health badge colors must meet contrast requirements (WCAG AA). Degraded vs misconfigured must be distinguishable without relying on hue alone.

Motion
- Avoid auto-animated charts that can be distracting; respect reduced-motion settings.

Copy
- Avoid ambiguous severity words; pair with actionable next step (“Check token”, “Confirm IAM role trust policy”).
deliverables: Figma: Audit Exports (Beta) — Settings IA + flows (page, empty state, list, details drawer)
Figma: Filter Builder component spec (states, validation, summary sentence, presets)
UX writing: beta disclaimers + status messaging snippets
Redlines: destination form field requirements and content rules
implementation_notes_for_eng:
Coordinate with Console team (Dylan Brooks / Chloe Martin / Svetlana Petrenko) on:
- Reusing existing Settings layout patterns (tables, drawers, empty states).
- Consistent secret input component (masked, rotate flow) with RBAC gating.
- Status endpoint data mapping (lag, last_success, last_error_code/message, paused state).
- Instrument UI events for funnel: view settings, add destination, test connection, save success/fail.

Design tokens
- Use standard badge component with explicit states; do not introduce custom colors outside design system.

Edge cases to handle in UI
- Feature flag disabled: show locked state and support contact path.
- User lacks permissions: read-only with clear “You do not have permission to edit audit exports” messaging.
- Destination unreachable / blocked by egress allowlist: show specific error code and doc link.
- Auto-paused by max lag safety: show banner with reason and next steps.
comments: 2025-02-12 (Tessa Morgan): Kicking off. Aligning on IA with Dylan/Chloe this week. Key open question: do we present filters on same page vs per-destination? Initial leaning: workspace-level filter applies to all destinations for beta (simpler mental model).

2025-02-18 (Naomi Feldman): Confirmed beta scope: workspace-level filter (applies to all destinations) is acceptable for v1; per-destination filters can be follow-on. Please ensure UI copy explicitly calls out at-least-once delivery + dedup via event_id.

2025-02-21 (Marcus Lin): Security asks that we avoid any UI affordance that implies exactly-once. Also: test events must be clearly labeled as synthetic and should not include customer PII. Add note in the design spec.
2025-02-26 (Alicia Perez): Drafted filter builder interaction model with presets and summary sentence. Avoiding free-form query language for beta; using structured selectors only.

2025-03-04 (Sean Gallagher): Status view should surface lag prominently; on-call will use dashboards but customers need self-serve signal. Suggest a simple badge + last success + lag number at minimum.
2025-03-07 (Dylan Brooks): Implementation note: we can likely ship destination details as a drawer first, not a full page. Please provide drawer redlines (width, sections, primary actions).

2025-03-11 (Alicia Perez): Updated designs to include: paused state banner, degraded badge copy examples, and link-out to docs/runbook. Added focus management + ARIA notes for chip removal and comboboxes.
2025-03-13 (Naomi Feldman): Approved with minor copy edits: replace “Replay” with “Backfill” everywhere; add max backfill limits in UI copy (PM will provide exact number once finalized).
2025-03-14 (Tessa Morgan): Design complete. Handing off to ENG-5177 for build. Please keep us in loop if backend constraints change (especially denylist support).

2025-04-28 (Alicia Perez): Post-beta feedback: customers struggled to find the last error details quickly. Proposed small tweak for GA: show last_error_code inline in list row subtitle. Logged note for follow-up ticket.
